timeline_reviews.summary: Transport-only serial Claude CLI stream; semantic events are projected from the raw project log.
Serial parent trajectory: probes executable behavior, writes all modules itself, runs differential and fuzz checks, verifies constraints, and exits with final response.

parallel.requirements: Recognized manual argv compatibility, construct Int8ul/Int16ul/Bytes build behavior, Python repr output, ESM .mjs structure, and no external dependencies.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent owned implementation and delegated semantic probing plus adversarial verification to workflows with multiple child attack lenses.
parallel.implementation: Built a broad runtime hierarchy for argparse, construct fields, Python integer parsing, repr, UTF-8, terminal width, stdio, and tracebacks.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Parent wrote and patched /output/test17.mjs and library files; artifact validation copied the expected entry despite no final response text.
parallel.verification: Ran curated cases, fuzzing, width sweeps, and verifier workflows; the verifier journal found divergences but aggregate verification did not return before kill.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluator passed 29/30 only; process return code 143 and killed final sweep show unresolved verification at closure.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same porting requirements and reference executable probing constraints from the prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Single agent owned probing, implementation, local test harnesses, constraint checks, and final response with no delegation.
serial.implementation: Built a smaller /output hierarchy covering construct, argparse, Python int/repr/traceback behavior, and the test17.mjs entry point.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Wrote the files directly under /output, patched one import, and delivered a final explanatory response.
serial.verification: Ran 58 differential cases, 600 randomized fuzz cases, help and stderr checks, sample cases, and import/forbidden-token checks.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluator also passed only 29/30, so a hidden mismatch remained despite clean local closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run recognized the same Py2JS task: pure Node ESM, .mjs files, manual argv parsing, exact construct output, no external dependencies, and output under /output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run received and followed the same prompt and source requirements for the construct/test17.py port.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No substantive requirement-recognition difference is evidenced; both failed one official case despite broad coverage.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent made task trackers and split semantic probing and adversarial verification into workflows while keeping implementation ownership in the parent.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent kept all probing, implementation, and verification in one trajectory without delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced workflow boundaries and child result lifecycles; serial had no handoff boundary and no child owner to join.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The verifier workflow was given the reference executable, /output/test17.mjs, exact comparison rules, and no-edit constraints.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run kept all task knowledge and implementation state locally while building the same module hierarchy.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The relevant contrast is not missing context but the lifecycle of returned verification findings across the workflow boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run iteratively patched argparse width behavior and terminal handling after probe feedback, building a larger runtime hierarchy.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run wrote a simpler hierarchy and then patched an import before using a local differential harness.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implemented broadly similar construct, Python-int, repr, traceback, and argparse behavior; parallel had more late patching pressure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent launched verifier work, later noted workflows were still running, and the verifier journal contained concrete findings but no completed aggregate reached the parent before closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run consumed its local test results directly: 58 differential cases passed and later 600 randomized cases passed before final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost a useful verifier return across the workflow boundary; serial had no child result lifecycle to complete.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel work mostly kept final writes in /output under the parent, but one shared /tmp fuzz harness was clobbered by a subagent and had to be relocated.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run used local /tmp harnesses and wrote /output modules itself with no competing child writes.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The /tmp collision disrupted parallel testing but was recovered and is not separately tied to the final official failure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verification included child adversarial findings plus parent tests, but final width-sweep verification was killed and the verifier aggregate never returned.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verification included a 58-case differential harness, 600 randomized cases, help output, stderr checks, sample runs, and a final summary.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial closed the verification loop locally; parallel left the strongest verifier feedback unresolved below workflow closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel agent consumed nearly the full 2400 second budget and exited with return code 143 after a killed final test command.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run exited normally with return code 0 in about 828 agent seconds and left substantial budget.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The process-level difference is closure: parallel was killed under budget pressure, while serial completed and produced a final response.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official status.json evaluation shows both modes failed at 29/30, so there is no discordant official outcome to explain. The concrete difference is that serial closed cleanly after local verification while parallel used workflows, received concrete verifier findings below the workflow, and was killed before a completed verifier return could be consumed.
parallel_contributors: Workflow-based verifier findings were trapped below parent closure.
Parallel process ended with return code 143 during final verification pressure.
serial_contributors: Serial verification stayed local and was consumed before final response.
Serial process exited cleanly with return code 0.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both solutions missed one hidden official case, and the raw pair does not expose which hidden testcase failed.
Parallel and serial implemented different support module structures but reached the same official 29/30 result.

candidates.reason: The parallel parent actively owned implementation and wrote the required output modules; the issue was not an unassigned implementation owner.
There were not multiple independently owned component implementations lacking a reconciler; the parent integrated code and probe findings itself.
The parent assembled and placed the required test17.mjs and libraries, and artifact validation found the expected entry file.
The parent created and managed implementation, semantic probing, fuzzing, and verification tasks, so the end-to-end pipeline had an owner despite later timeout.
Early probing informed the implementation but did not block all productive work behind one mandatory serial gate with idle capacity as the adverse event.
Investigation and implementation overlapped, including a launched semantic workflow while the parent continued coding; implementation was not deferred until a completed investigation phase.

The final implementation path received parent attention and produced an artifact; the directly evidenced adverse boundary is the verifier return lifecycle, not underallocation of implementation capacity.
The run used many child tokens and hit the budget, but excessive breadth is not proven as the qualifying direct cause of the verifier finding being trapped below the parent.
No single child received a demonstrably overbroad implementation scope that left indispensable work unfinished; verifier children were attack lenses rather than owners of the deliverable.
The executed probe and verifier children were given the task, reference executable, port path, no-Python rule, and comparison criteria; their issue was not following an incomplete brief.
Children were assigned probing and verification, not separately owned interoperating modules, so there is no incompatible component contract to reconcile.
No known finding is shown transferred and then omitted or truncated; the material verifier findings never reached the parent as a completed return.
The adverse result was not an oversized handoff that the parent could not reduce; the verifier aggregate result was absent.
The parent is not shown consuming a superseded child report that caused an inconsistent next action.
No incompatible returned reports reached the parent and remained unadjudicated at a decision point.
The parallel parent did not make a final whole-task acceptance decision; final.txt is empty and the process was killed, so evaluator failure alone cannot establish this label.
There is no replacement or retry child lacking inherited state and repeating prior work; provider retry count was one.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: No parent or orchestration action explicitly stopped an active child before its needed result; the observed terminal event is overall killed status.
A complete verifier-approved candidate or compatible component set was not ready for simple promotion before closure; unresolved verification findings remained.
No child implementation was merged only after relevant integrated verification; the observed issue is an unreturned verifier result.
The retained child work was verification, not a completed delegated implementation requiring parent adoption.

The parent launched a verifier workflow, but a verifier child produced concrete divergence findings in the workflow journal while the workflow state remained killed with a null aggregate result. The parent therefore never had a completed verifier return to consume before closure; serial verification stayed in the parent trajectory and was consumed before final response.
candidates.realized_consequence: Concrete verifier divergences were left below the workflow and could not be consumed as a completed parent-visible verification result before the parallel run was killed.
candidates.near_match_reason: Unused Completed Result would require a completed child result visible to the parent at a decision point; here the workflow aggregate was absent and the useful findings were trapped below the parent.

candidates.reason: The killed verifier workflow is part of the same lifecycle chain as the missing verifier return, and there is no separate child-failure takeover episode with a distinct consequence.
A completed verifier result was not parent-visible and ignored; the workflow state shows null aggregate result, making Missing Verifier Return more specific.
The parent inspected workflow journals and progress while waiting, so the adverse event was not waiting blindly without checking available state.
There were no separately owned source paths claiming overlapping final behavior that required unresolved design reconciliation.
No two live agents are shown editing the same final source or configuration file with one observing or reconciling the other change.
No non-entry source file produced or owned by another agent was wholesale replaced by the parent or a sibling.
The required submitted artifact test17.mjs was not overwritten by a competing child owner.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced multiple final outputs and invalidated another final-tree owner.
The children were instructed not to edit /output and the only observed shared-write problem was a temporary /tmp harness disturbance, not unstable final workspace provenance.
The parent observed that /tmp/fuzz.mjs had been clobbered and relocated its harness, but the final artifact is not shown to consume that temporary file as stable input or reference evidence.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Fan-out Budget Exhaustion was treated as a budget symptom without direct proof that breadth itself caused the trapped verifier return.
Blind Timeout Wait was rejected because the parent inspected workflow journals and progress.
No Failure Takeover was rejected as the same verifier closure chain rather than a separate consequence.
Artifact Leakage was rejected because the /tmp harness clobber was noticed and recovered without proven final-artifact contamination.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 L2 rows and all 32 L3 candidates were audited; only the verifier return lifecycle cleared the paired retention gate.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: Downstream timeout, aborted workflow, and missing takeover symptoms were not split into extra labels around the same episode.
